study: Federated optimiser comparison (FedAvg / FedAdam / FedProx) with a predeclared label-free stopping rule, plus a model-depth arm, 2026-09-29
classification: Exploratory healthy-only development on the previously opened LDM-free 54-client cohort. Not independent validation.
questions: Q1 (primary): does the federated optimiser change strict device-level detection when each is stopped by the same label-free rule?
Q2: how many communication rounds does each optimiser need under that rule, and what does that cost in LoRaWAN fragments?
Q3 (secondary): does a deeper autoencoder (22-16-8-16-22) change detection relative to H12 (22-12-22)?

cohort.exclusion: manifest filtered by dataset before any cache load, identical to healthy_only_causal_no_ldm_20260922

data: Existing healthy_only_suite_20260907 cache and partitions; no new data, no downloads.
activation: tanh on every hidden layer, linear output
initialisation: per layer normal(0, sqrt(2/(fan_in+fan_out))), zero biases, drawn sequentially from one seeded generator; identical to wider_models for h12
local_training: full-batch gradient descent on the client's TRAINING rows only; loss = mean squared reconstruction error + 0.5*L2*sum(W^2); lr 0.03; L2 1e-4; 2 local epochs per round; identical for every algorithm
client_weighting: equal (unweighted mean over clients) for every algorithm, matching the reported configuration

algorithms.fedavg: server model = old + mean(client_model - old), i.e. the unweighted mean of client models (McMahan et al. 2017)
algorithms.fedadam: server-side Adam on the mean client delta with bias correction: eta 0.01, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.99, tau 0.001 (Reddi et al. 2021); identical to wider_models
algorithms.fedprox: FedAvg aggregation; each client adds (mu/2)*||w - w_global||^2 to its local loss (Li et al. 2020). PRIMARY mu = 0.01. Sensitivity mu in {0.001, 0.1, 1.0} is reported for h12 only and is never used to pick a winner.

stopping_rule.signal: healthy validation loss = unweighted mean over clients of each client's reconstruction MSE on its own CALIBRATION rows. Calibration rows are healthy commissioning data; no fault label, onset or test row is used. In deployment each client would report this as one scalar alongside its update.
stopping_rule.rule: Let B_t be the best (minimum) validation loss observed up to and including round t. Stop at the first round t >= P+1 for which (B_{t-P} - B_t) / B_{t-P} < epsilon. The model deployed is the model at round t (not the best-so-far), because a node cannot hold a history of models.
stopping_rule.if_never_triggered: stop at max_rounds and report the stop as 'cap'
stopping_rule.causality: Training always continues to max_rounds so curves can be reported, but the stop decision at round t uses only B_1..B_t. Continuing past the stop cannot influence which model is evaluated.

evaluation.score: per-acquisition reconstruction MSE of the global model on the device-local standardised 22 features
evaluation.alarm_layer: unchanged frozen layer: dense cadence, causal 13-of-21 trailing order statistic, reference = max over training+calibration history, multiplier 2.0, suppressed through end of calibration
evaluation.route: single global-model route only; no PCA conjunction, so the comparison isolates the optimiser
evaluation.strict_success: scored device with no alarm in the healthy test period AND an alarm in the fault period; a control succeeds by never alarming
checkpoints_reported: at round 12 (comparability with the reported configuration)

communication_accounting: per client per round = uplink + downlink fragments, each ceil((4*parameters + 16) / 200) at float32. h12: 12 + 12 = 24 fragments per round. deep: 21 + 21 = 42 fragments per round.
replication_gate: BEFORE any new outcome is computed: fedadam on h12 at round 12 must reproduce the saved LDM-free global_h12 weights for every seed to within 1e-10, and its evaluation must reproduce 45/49, 44/49, 44/49. Failure aborts the study with nothing written except the failure.

decision_rules_fixed_in_advance.detection: One optimiser is 'better for detection' only if its strict count at the stopping round is >= the other's on all three seeds and strictly greater on at least two. Otherwise they are reported as not distinguishable.
decision_rules_fixed_in_advance.communication: One optimiser is 'cheaper' only if it stops in fewer rounds on all three seeds.
decision_rules_fixed_in_advance.recommendation: Prefer the cheaper optimiser unless another is better for detection under the rule above.
decision_rules_fixed_in_advance.depth: The deeper model is 'better' only if, under the same optimiser, its strict count is >= h12's on all three seeds and strictly greater on at least two. A deeper model that is not better is rejected on communication cost.

known_limitations: Relative-improvement stopping can stop a slow optimiser early. The round-60 checkpoint is reported so a premature stop is visible.
Stopping and threshold calibration both use calibration rows. Both are healthy data and label-free, but it is a double use of one partition and is stated as such.
With only 2 full-batch local epochs, client drift is small, so FedProx is expected to behave close to FedAvg. That is a property of the configuration, not evidence against FedProx in general.
Three seeds. A one-device difference is inside seed spread and is not a finding.
